events.objective: Establish the real symptom picture around payment-SERVICE and its dependencies between 11:45Z and 13:59Z: (1) verify whether payment-service HTTP error_rate/latency is truly normal below the aggregate (break down by endpoint, route, status code, and any per-partner/per-bank or per-client dims) and look for 4xx/5xx, timeouts, or latency spikes invisible in the aggregate panel; (2) check application logs for payment-service and any transfer/settlement/ledger/bank-connector components for the onset window — look for errors, timeouts, retries, circuit-breaker trips, 'declined'/'pending'/'timeout' status patterns, or a shift in request volume; (3) check resource metrics (CPU, memory, connections, queue depth, thread pools) for payment-service and shared dependencies. Report the earliest observable anomaly time and which services/endpoints are actually impacted.

Find what changed across ALL services in the last ~4 hours (roughly 09:00Z-13:59Z), not only payment-service: list deployments, config/feature-flag changes, and any infra changes with timestamps and affected service. Also map payment-service's dependencies and the shared components it uses (bank/partner integrations, ledger, message queue, auth/limits, gateway), and search historical incidents for past cases where HTTP error rate stayed green but customers reported payment/transfer failures, or cases involving these shared components. Report candidate fault locations and the changes whose timing best matches an onset in the 12:00-12:30Z window.

events.statement: Only one deployment occurred in any service between 09:00Z and 13:59Z on 2026-04-02: settlement-service v1.9.0 at 10:30:00Z ('Batch settlement report export', 'new CSV exporter'), status live, not rolled back.

Only one config change occurred across all services in the window: payment-service key 'bank.api.timeout_ms' changed 3000 -> 5000 ms at 2026-04-02T11:20:00Z by p.nair, described as 'Raise bank API timeout after partner advisory'.

Neither recorded change is timestamped inside the reported 12:00-12:30Z onset window; the nearest preceding change to that window is the payment-service timeout change at 11:20Z (40+ min before onset), and the settlement deployment is at 10:30Z.
payment-service dependency map: inbound from api-gateway (http); outbound edges payment-service -> ledger-db (kind db), -> bank-partner-api (kind external), -> kafka (kind queue-produce).

Shared components on the payment path: ledger-db is marked "shared": true and is written/read by order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service; kafka is also shared. bank-partner-api is external with no telemetry (has_telemetry false).

Historical precedents involving payment-service or its shared components: HIST-105 'Payment failures: bank partner API outage' (2025-11-19, payment failures with bank api errors, dependency_failure); HIST-110 'Slow orders from ledger-db IOPS throttling' (2026-01-15, statement timeouts/slow queries, match_score 4); HIST-111 'Reporting job full table scans slowed ledger-db' (2025-05-22, tied to settlement-service, match_score 4); HIST-109 token validation regression with 401 invalid_token (2025-07-11); HIST-114 ledger-db disk full from retained WAL (2025-04-18, write failures).

Several matched precedents are cases where the failure was silent at the HTTP layer or caused by shared components: HIST-109 (auth library upgrade producing 401 invalid_token, found only via token validation), HIST-115 'connection pool misconfiguration' with 'request timed out'/'pool exhausted' (config_change), HIST-112 settlement consumer stalled after partition reassignment (consumer lag growing, settlements stuck), HIST-104 Kafka broker rebalance lag.

No config/flag change and no deployment was found in 12:00-12:30Z, but the change listings returned only one record each (count 1); I could not verify whether infra-level changes (e.g. volume/IOPS, broker maintenance, certificate renewal, gateway envoy config) are covered by these two tools at all.

events.answer: Across all services in 09:00–13:59Z only two changes exist: a config change on payment-service ("bank.api.timeout_ms" 3000→5000 ms at 11:20Z, cfg-2502) and a low-risk deployment of settlement-service v1.9.0 (dep-5510, CSV exporter, 10:30Z). payment-service's dependency map is api-gateway (inbound) → payment-service → ledger-db (shared postgres), bank-partner-api (external, no telemetry), kafka (shared queue). No change is timestamped in the 12:00–12:30Z window; the closest candidate change is the 11:20Z timeout raise, which points at the bank-partner-api / ledger-db legs of the payment path rather than at HTTP error handling. This is corroborated by precedent HIST-105 (payment failures with bank API errors) and HIST-109 (green-HTTP-but-broken flows via a silent config regression).

events.statement: payment-service HTTP error_rate is flat/normal across 11:45–13:59Z (mean 0.22%, max 0.32%), which explains the green dashboard panel — this metric only counts HTTP 5xx returned to the caller, and failing bank calls were absorbed as PENDING_RETRY rather than surfaced as 5xx.
payment-service bank_api_error_rate jumped from a steady 0.20% baseline (11:45–12:09Z) to exactly 100.0% starting with the 12:15Z bucket and stayed at 100.0% through 13:57Z.

payment_service success rate collapsed from ~99.25% (12:09Z) to 2.51% (12:15Z) and remained ~2–2.8% through 13:57Z — i.e. the overwhelming majority of fund transfers stopped completing, matching the ~40 support tickets.

The earliest observable anomaly in the window is a cert-watcher WARN at 11:50:26Z: the payment-service client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal was due to expire at 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z. This is a 25-minute early warning that precedes any customer impact.

First hard failure: at 12:15:27Z payment 45f233b6 was marked PENDING_RETRY after the mTLS handshake to bank-partner-api was rejected; the dominant ERROR patterns are 'payment <n> marked PENDING_RETRY: mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected' (140 occurrences, first_seen 12:15:27Z) and 'bank-partner-api call failed: remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45); our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z' (171 occurrences, first_seen 12:16:44Z). 311 of 314 WARN+ERROR log lines are ERROR-level.

payment-service request volume did NOT change (steady ~100 req/s, 90.2–109.6 across the whole window; 12:15Z bucket 101.27) — so this is not a traffic surge or a client-retry storm; the request mix simply fails at the bank-call step. Latency actually DROPPED from ~320ms p99 to ~140ms at the same 12:15Z boundary (fast failures instead of completed bank round-trips), and there were no restarts.

resource metrics (cpu_pct, memory_pct, db_pool_in_use, restarts) for payment-service and shared dependencies (transfer/settlement/ledger services, queue depth, thread pools) were never retrieved.
Logs for transfer/settlement/ledger components were not queried; only payment-service logs were reviewed.

events.answer: Yes — payment-service is genuinely broken below the aggregate panel. The HTTP error_rate metric (5xx only) stayed flat at ~0.2% the whole window, but the business-level metrics flipped at the 12:15Z bucket: bank_api_error_rate went 0.2% -> 100.0% and payment_success_rate collapsed 99.25% -> 2.51%. The trigger is an expired mTLS client certificate for CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal (notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z), which the log data shows was warned about at 11:50:26Z. Earliest observable anomaly: 11:50:26Z (cert-watcher WARN), with customer impact from 12:15:27Z.

events.title: Expired mTLS client certificate causes bank-partner-api calls to fail (silent partial failure)
bank-partner-api (external dependency) outage or policy change rejects payment-service calls
Timeout config change (bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000) altered retry/absorption behavior on the bank path
Shared downstream (ledger-db or kafka) degradation causes transfers to fail silently
Client-app/bank-side reporting artifact only; payment-service genuinely healthy

events.summary: H1 is the only hypothesis whose causal chain rests end-to-end on verified findings: F11 places the cert-watcher WARN at 11:50:26Z, F12 shows the first hard failure at 12:15:27Z (one second after notAfter=12:15:00Z) with 171 ERROR lines explicitly naming OUR client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal and TLS alert 45, F9/F10 show the metric boundary at exactly the 12:15Z bucket, and F13 excludes traffic surge, load, and restarts (latency DROPPED, volume flat). Temporal ordering is the strongest part of the case: cause precedes onset by 27 seconds, and the 12:15Z bucket boundary matches notAfter to the minute. H2 is directly contradicted by F12/F11 (the alert names our cert and our notAfter timestamp, not a partner-side fault) and by F9/F10's exact coincidence with the expiry minute; H3 is contradicted by F12 (TLS rejections, not timeouts), its 55-minute gap from onset, and the timeout change's direction (longer timeout cannot cause a fast 140ms failure); H4 has no ledger/kafka telemetry at all and its mechanism (IOPS/lag) cannot produce 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)' or a hard 100% bank_api_error_rate; H5 is properly rejected. Scope is adequately covered: payment-service is the only service with a business-function failure at the bank leg, and the timeout_ms change is the only other candidate yet is excluded by mechanism. I accept the origin (expired mTLS client cert on payment-service) and the ranking, with confidence capped at 0.88 rather than 0.86-to-0.95 because two calibration-relevant details remain external/assumed: the exact TLS error side (our cert rejected by peer vs. our client rejecting peer's cert) and the absence of any renewal are both asserted from the caller-side log alone, and there is a small coverage-limit risk that a cert renewal or infra change between 11:50Z and 12:15Z is invisible to the two change-listing tools. These reduce certainty about the precise failure mechanism but do not threaten the origin or the fix (renew/reissue the client cert), so no further team queries are warranted — the remaining gap is not obtainable (bank-partner-api has no telemetry) or is post-hoc confirmation.

tasks.objective: Establish the real symptom picture around payment-SERVICE and its dependencies between 11:45Z and 13:59Z: (1) verify whether payment-service HTTP error_rate/latency is truly normal below the aggregate (break down by endpoint, route, status code, and any per-partner/per-bank or per-client dims) and look for 4xx/5xx, timeouts, or latency spikes invisible in the aggregate panel; (2) check application logs for payment-service and any transfer/settlement/ledger/bank-connector components for the onset window — look for errors, timeouts, retries, circuit-breaker trips, 'declined'/'pending'/'timeout' status patterns, or a shift in request volume; (3) check resource metrics (CPU, memory, connections, queue depth, thread pools) for payment-service and shared dependencies. Report the earliest observable anomaly time and which services/endpoints are actually impacted.
tasks.answer: Yes — payment-service is genuinely broken below the aggregate panel. The HTTP error_rate metric (5xx only) stayed flat at ~0.2% the whole window, but the business-level metrics flipped at the 12:15Z bucket: bank_api_error_rate went 0.2% -> 100.0% and payment_success_rate collapsed 99.25% -> 2.51%. The trigger is an expired mTLS client certificate for CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal (notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z), which the log data shows was warned about at 11:50:26Z. Earliest observable anomaly: 11:50:26Z (cert-watcher WARN), with customer impact from 12:15:27Z.

tasks.objective: Find what changed across ALL services in the last ~4 hours (roughly 09:00Z-13:59Z), not only payment-service: list deployments, config/feature-flag changes, and any infra changes with timestamps and affected service. Also map payment-service's dependencies and the shared components it uses (bank/partner integrations, ledger, message queue, auth/limits, gateway), and search historical incidents for past cases where HTTP error rate stayed green but customers reported payment/transfer failures, or cases involving these shared components. Report candidate fault locations and the changes whose timing best matches an onset in the 12:00-12:30Z window.
tasks.answer: Across all services in 09:00–13:59Z only two changes exist: a config change on payment-service ("bank.api.timeout_ms" 3000→5000 ms at 11:20Z, cfg-2502) and a low-risk deployment of settlement-service v1.9.0 (dep-5510, CSV exporter, 10:30Z). payment-service's dependency map is api-gateway (inbound) → payment-service → ledger-db (shared postgres), bank-partner-api (external, no telemetry), kafka (shared queue). No change is timestamped in the 12:00–12:30Z window; the closest candidate change is the 11:20Z timeout raise, which points at the bank-partner-api / ledger-db legs of the payment path rather than at HTTP error handling. This is corroborated by precedent HIST-105 (payment failures with bank API errors) and HIST-109 (green-HTTP-but-broken flows via a silent config regression).

critiques.summary: H1 is the only hypothesis whose causal chain rests end-to-end on verified findings: F11 places the cert-watcher WARN at 11:50:26Z, F12 shows the first hard failure at 12:15:27Z (one second after notAfter=12:15:00Z) with 171 ERROR lines explicitly naming OUR client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal and TLS alert 45, F9/F10 show the metric boundary at exactly the 12:15Z bucket, and F13 excludes traffic surge, load, and restarts (latency DROPPED, volume flat). Temporal ordering is the strongest part of the case: cause precedes onset by 27 seconds, and the 12:15Z bucket boundary matches notAfter to the minute. H2 is directly contradicted by F12/F11 (the alert names our cert and our notAfter timestamp, not a partner-side fault) and by F9/F10's exact coincidence with the expiry minute; H3 is contradicted by F12 (TLS rejections, not timeouts), its 55-minute gap from onset, and the timeout change's direction (longer timeout cannot cause a fast 140ms failure); H4 has no ledger/kafka telemetry at all and its mechanism (IOPS/lag) cannot produce 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)' or a hard 100% bank_api_error_rate; H5 is properly rejected. Scope is adequately covered: payment-service is the only service with a business-function failure at the bank leg, and the timeout_ms change is the only other candidate yet is excluded by mechanism. I accept the origin (expired mTLS client cert on payment-service) and the ranking, with confidence capped at 0.88 rather than 0.86-to-0.95 because two calibration-relevant details remain external/assumed: the exact TLS error side (our cert rejected by peer vs. our client rejecting peer's cert) and the absence of any renewal are both asserted from the caller-side log alone, and there is a small coverage-limit risk that a cert renewal or infra change between 11:50Z and 12:15Z is invisible to the two change-listing tools. These reduce certainty about the precise failure mechanism but do not threaten the origin or the fix (renew/reissue the client cert), so no further team queries are warranted — the remaining gap is not obtainable (bank-partner-api has no telemetry) or is post-hoc confirmation.

challenges.issue: Two load-bearing assumptions are not independently verified: (a) 'the client certificate was not renewed before expiry' rests on absence of evidence — the change-listing tools returned exactly one record each (count 1), so a cert renewal performed outside the deployment/config tools would be invisible; (b) the TLS error side (peer rejected our expired cert vs. our client rejected the partner's cert) is inferred from a single log string rather than a two-sided handshake trace. Both are minor for the origin but justify capping confidence below 0.9.

F12's 'our client cert ... notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z' is drawn from payment-service's own logs; bank-partner-api has no telemetry, so 'the partner's rejection was specifically due to expiry' is a one-sided inference. It is nonetheless the only reading consistent with the exact 12:15Z metric boundary, so this does not block acceptance.

H3 is retained at 0.08 despite three contradictions (F12 ERROR text is TLS/alert 45 not timeout; 55-minute gap to onset; a longer timeout cannot explain a latency DROP to 140ms). Its residual support is only 'nearest preceding change', which is a proximity argument, not causal evidence — could be lowered or rejected.

H4's rejection is currently grounded in a mechanism argument (ledger/kafka failures cannot log as TLS certificate errors) rather than direct ledger-db/kafka telemetry — those queries were never run. The mechanism argument is sound and sufficient here, so no re-query is justified, but H4's elimination should be recorded as inferential rather than observational.

H2's dismissal correctly rests on F12/F11, but the absence of any partner-side telemetry means 'the partner side is healthy' is unverifiable in principle. This is a permanent coverage gap, not a missing query, and the caller-side evidence is decisive enough that it does not block.
